root_cause.text: The `__arm_lpae_unmap()` function in the ARM LPAE io-pgtable driver returns a negative error code (`-ENOENT`) despite having an unsigned return type (`size_t`), resulting in an integer signedness conversion bug that propagates a huge positive value.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows that when encountering an unmapped page table entry (`!pte`), `__arm_lpae_unmap()` returns `-ENOENT`, which is then corrected to `return 0;`. The commit message confirms that "Since size_t is unsigned, -ENOENT (typically -2) becomes a huge positive value (0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFE on 64-bit systems)" which propagates through the call chain and triggers a `BUG_ON` in `iommu_pgsize()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix __arm_lpae_unmap to return 0 instead of -ENOENT when a page table entry is already empty.
intent_record.what: The return value of the __arm_lpae_unmap function when encountering an empty page table entry is changed from -ENOENT to 0.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that the function correctly returns 0 bytes unmapped instead of a large unsigned integer value caused by casting the negative error code -ENOENT to size_t.

grouping_result.intent: Fix __arm_lpae_unmap to return 0 instead of -ENOENT when a page table entry is already empty.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the vulnerability by changing the return value of __arm_lpae_unmap from -ENOENT (which causes a signedness conversion bug due to the size_t return type) to 0.

candidates.rationale: The function __arm_lpae_unmap has a return type of size_t (unsigned). Returning -ENOENT (a negative integer) causes it to be implicitly cast to a very large unsigned value, leading to incorrect unmap size propagation.

Since the function `__arm_lpae_unmap` has a return type of `size_t` (as shown on line 639), returning a negative error code like `-ENOENT` causes an implicit conversion to a very large unsigned integer, leading to the described integer signedness conversion bug.

Author: Will Deacon <will@kernel.org>
Date:   Fri Nov 14 17:18:23 2014 +0000

    iommu: add ARM LPAE page table allocator
    
    A number of IOMMUs found in ARM SoCs can walk architecture-compatible
    page tables.
    
    This patch adds a generic allocator for Stage-1 and Stage-2 v7/v8
    long-descriptor page tables. 4k, 16k and 64k pages are supported, with
    up to 4-levels of walk to cover a 48-bit address space.
    
    Tested-by: Lau
